label: early original-phase input of e/d/w/y/h/m (at most one earlier letter)
explanation: Most of the mass (72%) is in the original phase at t=0-3. It fires when the input is one of e, d, w, y, h, m (about 3x lift each) near the start of the sequence, with at most one letter before it (digits before it do not count). At t=0 one of these tokens always activates it (precision 1.0), but those activations are weak (17% of mass). The strongest activations come at t=1-2, especially after a leading digit like 0 or z (e.g. 0 0 e, z 0 y d). Activation fades fast after t=3 and is almost zero for orig_idx>=5. It rarely fires on the <DEL> step. A secondary weaker copy-phase component (about 26% of mass) favors outputs p, j, f, 1, z, c at middle recall positions, but adding it hurt F1 because precision is low. The predicate misses this copy-phase activity and some early activations on other tokens (e.g. m q after 0). Dev F1 0.59, mass recall 0.47.
